title: Trans-regulatory gene mapping prioritizes disease drivers in asthma.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: GEO esummary for the 4 linked series: GSE329629 (SuperSeries, 23 samples), GSE329569 (CRISPR screen, 12 samples), GSE329488 (Th2 RNA-seq, 4 samples), GSE329487 (RNA-seq, 7 samples). Downloaded GSE329569_read_counts.txt.gz (24 KB): 536 sgRNA (guide RNA) rows covering 133 genes, 12 count columns (4 replicates x low/mid/high sorted bins). Listed the two RNA-seq count files (1.4 MB, 1.5 MB) without opening.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Full text was not retrievable (Europe PMC 500 error; supplement endpoint returned no zip). From the abstract and text-mined accessions: the DANDELION gene scores combine trans-eQTL (expression quantitative trait locus) effects, likely from GSE158752 airway data, with whole-exome burden statistics, plausibly from UK Biobank (controlled access) and GWAS Catalog summary statistics (GCST90002400 etc.). The per-gene DPG (disease-proximal gene) score table was not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: GEO count files download openly (checked). The exome burden input is likely controlled-access UK Biobank; not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only measured label in the files is CRISPR screen guide counts in sorted bins; a hit/no-hit label would have to be computed from them. The DPG prioritization is a statistical score, not a measured column, and wasn't found in the files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene symbols are present in the screen file (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: The screen covers 133 genes with 536 guides (counted in the file), far under the ~400-row minimum for classification. The RNA-seq series have 4 to 7 samples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: All processed files are under 2 MB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Couldn't check: no full text to compare against.

a8_label_provenance.note: A DPG label would be the output of the DANDELION statistical model, so training on it would distil that model (circular).

honest_claim_h3: With 133 screened genes, a model could at most claim it ranks which of a hand-picked asthma gene set changes a cell phenotype, and that sample is too small to support the claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene-level genetic and regulatory features to predict which genes change asthma-related cell behaviour when knocked out.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-gene features such as regulatory effect sizes and exome burden for the 133 genes in the CRISPR screen (counted in the file).
plain_idea.predict: Whether knocking out the gene shifts guide counts across sorted cell bins in the CRISPR (gene-editing) screen.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would help asthma geneticists decide which candidate genes to test in the lab, but 133 pre-selected genes is too few to learn from.

ml_idea: None viable. The open data is one 133-gene CRISPR screen plus small RNA-seq sets (4 to 7 samples); the gene-prioritization score is a model output, and its exome inputs are likely controlled access.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because Part A failed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the genes in the CRISPR screen file: 133 genes, done, which kills it.

verdict_reason: Fails A5, A2 and A8. The open files are a 133-gene CRISPR screen (536 guides, verified) and RNA-seq with 4 to 7 samples. The gene-priority label is a statistical model's output, and its exome input is likely controlled-access UK Biobank.
